details: The Federal Reserve is set to release the minutes from its June 16-17 FOMC meeting today, July 8, 2026. These minutes will provide detailed insights into policymakers' perspectives on inflation, the labor market, and the necessity for further monetary tightening. The tone of the minutes – whether hawkish (suggesting sustained higher rates) or dovish (hinting at earlier easing) – is expected to significantly impact the trajectory of interest rates and, consequently, the volatility of cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum.
title: FOMC Minutes Expected to Influence Crypto Volatility

details: Renewed geopolitical tensions have rattled global markets, with Brent crude oil surging over 2% following US airstrikes on Iran and the revocation of waivers that allowed Tehran to sell oil internationally. This escalation in the Middle East has reignited inflation concerns, leading Bitcoin to fall by approximately 1.5%. The cryptocurrency's reaction suggests it is currently behaving more like a high-beta liquidity asset sensitive to risk appetite rather than a traditional safe haven.
title: Geopolitical Tensions Drive Oil Surge, Bitcoin Decline

details: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has formally included three crypto-related items in its 2026 regulatory agenda. This move signifies a notable pivot under Chairman Paul Atkins, prioritizing formal rulemaking over an enforcement-heavy approach. The agenda aims to establish clearer federal rules for digital assets by proposing amendments to regulations for exchanges and broker-dealers, which could foster a more predictable and stable regulatory environment for the crypto market.
title: SEC Signals Shift Towards Clearer Crypto Regulations in 2026 Agenda

details: The transitional period for the European Union's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) officially concluded on July 1, 2026. EU lawmakers have now adopted a comprehensive digital asset policy stance, encompassing assessments for decentralized finance (DeFi), staking, crypto lending, and non-fungible tokens (NFTs). This regulatory clarity is expected to further integrate digital assets into traditional financial and regulatory frameworks across the European Economic Area.
title: EU MiCA Regulation Transition Period Concludes

details: Bitcoin experienced a nearly 7% rise over the week ending July 5, marking its strongest weekly performance since March. This rally was primarily fueled by declining inflation expectations, with the two-year breakeven inflation rate falling below the Federal Reserve's 2% target. A concurrent decrease in WTI crude oil prices has prompted markets to reassess inflationary pressures and expectations for future interest rate cuts, contributing to a positive sentiment for risk assets like Bitcoin.
title: Bitcoin Rallies on Declining Inflation Expectations

details: MicroStrategy recently disclosed a sale of 3,588 BTC, amounting to $216 million, as part of its updated treasury management strategy. While historically such sales might trigger significant market movements, the reaction this time was notably muted. This event is being closely watched by investors as corporate treasuries re-evaluate their Bitcoin holdings, signifying a potential shift in how large institutional holders manage their digital assets for liquidity purposes.
title: MicroStrategy's Bitcoin Sale Meets Muted Market Reaction

details: Former U.S. President Donald Trump has reiterated his strong support for cryptocurrencies, even hinting at the potential inclusion of Bitcoin in a U.S. Treasury-linked digital asset account. These comments have positively influenced market sentiment, leading to a surge in Bitcoin's price and related crypto stocks. His statements underscore the significant impact political figures can have on the perception and valuation of digital assets.
title: Trump Expresses Strong Support for Cryptocurrencies
